name: Unifocal Peripheral Venous Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of a soft, compressible, bluish lesion localized to peripheral tissues
MRI showing slow-flow venous channels without arterial involvement
Doppler ultrasound confirming absence of arterial flow within the lesion
Histological confirmation of dilated venous channels lined by flattened endothelium

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus imaging characteristics demonstrating slow-flow venous malformation without arterial involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not mandatory if imaging and clinical features are conclusive

pathognomonic.symptomName: Soft, compressible bluish cutaneous or subcutaneous lesion
searchTerms: soft, bluish, squishy skin or under skin lump

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lesion enlargement with dependent positioning or Valsalva maneuver
searchTerms: lesion gets bigger when standing or straining
swelling increases with position changes or Valsalva
mass enlarges with dependent posture or straining

common.symptomName: Localized pain or tenderness at lesion site
Swelling or palpable mass in affected peripheral area
searchTerms: swelling or lump in limb or peripheral area
palpable mass in arm or leg
visible dilated veins on skin surface
skin darkening or redness on lesion

occasional.symptomName: Localized muscle weakness adjacent to lesion
searchTerms: localized weakness adjacent to affected area
reduced muscle strength next to lesion

occasional.symptomName: Functional impairment due to lesion size or location

searchTerms: tingling or numbness from nerve pressure

laboratory: Normal coagulation profile unless thrombophlebitis present
D-dimer may be elevated in cases with thrombosis
imaging: MRI demonstrating slow-flow venous channels with characteristic T2 hyperintensity
Doppler ultrasound showing absence of arterial flow and compressible venous structures
Phlebography may show dilated venous lakes
genetic: Somatic mutations in TEK (TIE2) gene reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing dilated, thin-walled venous channels lined by endothelial cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mixed vascular channels including capillary and lymphatic components
Different imaging characteristics with lymphatic fluid components
Imaging shows arterial feeders and early venous drainage

redFlags: Severe pain disproportionate to lesion size
